comparison_summary: supragingival therapy vs intensive therapy
intervention_description: All individuals were given oral hygiene instructions. The supragingival therapy group (ST, n = 12) received supragingival scaling using an ultrasonic device and periodontal curettes (Hu-Friedy®, Chicago, USA). A Single appointment lasted ~ 60 minutes. Supportive therapy for biofilm control consisted of professional instructions on oral hygiene given to each patient every month.

comparison_summary: supragingival therapy vs intensive therapy
intervention_description: All individuals were given oral hygiene instructions. The intensive therapy group (IT, n = 12) received supra- and subgingival scaling and root planing, (in sites with PPD ≥ 4 mm) using an ultrasonic device and periodontal curettes. The procedures for the IT group were performed under local anesthesia (3% prilocaine with felypressin), in two appointments lasting ~ 120 minutes each. Supportive therapy for biofilm control consisted of professional instructions on oral hygiene given to each patient every month.

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRP and doxycycline vs no periodontal treatment
intervention_description: The subjects in group I received oral hygiene instructions and full mouth SRP

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRP and doxycycline vs no periodontal treatment
intervention_description: subjects in group II received doxycycline (DOXT, Dr Reddy's Lab. Ltd, Hyderabad, India) (total dose 1,600 mg in equally divided 16 doses, start as 100 mg BD followed by OD for 14 days) in addition to the same therapy as that of group I.

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRP and doxycycline vs no periodontal treatment
intervention_description: The group III received no treatment that served as control.

comparison_summary: supragingival prophylaxis vs that of subgingival debridement for supportive periodontal care
intervention_description: Patients in treatment group 1 received non-surgical periodontal treatment, which consisted of scaling and root planing under local anesthesia at baseline and additional subgingival debridement at the 3-month follow-up.

comparison_summary: supragingival prophylaxis vs that of subgingival debridement for supportive periodontal care
intervention_description: Those in treatment group 2 underwent non-surgical periodontal treatment at the initial visit and only supragingival prophylaxis, with no intervention in deep periodontal pockets at 3 months.

comparison_summary: supragingival prophylaxis vs that of subgingival debridement for supportive periodontal care
intervention_description: Those in the control group received no treatment measure or formal oral hygiene instructions until the end of the study.

comparison_summary: intensive periodontal therapy vs usual care
intervention_description: whole mouth subgingival scaling, surgical periodontal therapy [if the participants showed good oral hygiene practice; otherwise dental cleaning again], and supportive periodontal therapy every 3 months until completion of the study

comparison_summary: intensive periodontal therapy vs usual care
intervention_description: supra-gingival scaling and polishing at the same timepoints as in the IPT group

comparison_summary: nonsurgical periodontal therapy vs no therapy
intervention_description: Initial treatment consisted of at least 160 minutes of scaling and root planing using currettes and ultrasonic instruments with local anesthesia during 2 or more sessions completed within 42 days of the baseline visit. Completeness of therapy was assessed by the study therapist and confirmed by a study periodontist. After treatment, the therapist provided oral hygiene instructions and dispensed chlorhexidine gluconate (0.12% oral rinse, twice daily for 2 weeks), toothbrush, toothpaste, and dental floss. Three and 6 months after the baseline visit, participants in the treatment group received oral hygiene instructions and scaling and root planing for approximately 1 hour during a single session.

comparison_summary: nonsurgical periodontal therapy vs no therapy
intervention_description: Participants in the control group received only oral hygiene instructions at the baseline and 3- and 6-month visits.

comparison_summary: scaling and root planing and oral hygiene instructions vs the control group which only received oral hygiene instructions
intervention_description: Scaling and root planing was performed with an ultrasonic scaler (Dentsply, York, PA, USA) and Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy, Chicago, IL, USA). Two quadrants were instrumented at each appointment under local anaesthesia

comparison_summary: scaling and root planing and oral hygiene instructions vs the control group which only received oral hygiene instructions
intervention_description: the control group which only received oral hygiene instructions.

comparison_summary: immediate periodontal therapy vs delayed periodontal therapy
intervention_description: Periodontal therapy included scaling and root planing (SRP), the combination of systemic antibiotics metronidazole 400 mg three times daily for two weeks and amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily for 2 weeks (Miranda et al., 2014), and oral hygiene instructions (OHI). Full-mouth SRP was performed by the same specialist (MY) for all patients in the test group using ultrasonic apparatus (Cavitron Select SPC, Dentsply professional) and Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy) in a single two-hour session. Local anesthesia was applied when needed. SRP was associated with subgingival irrigation by chlorhexidine 0.12% mouthwash (Peridex oral rinse, 3M ESPE Dental Products).

comparison_summary: immediate periodontal therapy vs delayed periodontal therapy
intervention_description: For the patients within the control group, delayed periodontal therapy was performed using the same procedures that were applied for the patients in the test group exactly after the end of follow-up period (3 months) because of ethical reasons. Therefore, within the control group, no periodontal therapies were done during the follow-up.

arm_label: T2DM - Tooth extraction and periodontal treatment (FM-SRP)
comparison_summary: surgical treatment (tooth extraction) alone or in combination with non-surgical periodontal treatment (tooth cleaning)
intervention_description: At least one tooth extraction was performed for each patient. Prior to the surgical procedures, an adjunctive, non-surgical periodontal treatment to achieve a full-mouth tooth cleaning was performed for the patients in the treatment groups: Full-Mouth Scaling and Root Planning (FM-SRP) using an ultrasonic device (UDS-J Ultrasonic Scaler, Guilin Woodpecker Medical Instrument) and periodontal currettes for the mechanical debridement of supra- and subgingival plaque and calculus. Post-operative rinsing was followed by the use of the antiseptic solution Listerine® (ethanol 21.6%, methyl salicylate 0.06%, menthol 0.042%, thymol 0.064% and eucalyptol 0.092%) as a mouthwash thrice a day for 3 w.

comparison_summary: surgical treatment (tooth extraction) alone or in combination with non-surgical periodontal treatment (tooth cleaning)
intervention_description: At least one tooth was extracted from each patient. After extraction, the control group (n=50) did not receive any other treatment until the 3-month follow-up.

arm_label: Non-Diabetic - Tooth extraction and periodontal treatment (FM-SRP)

comparison_summary: full-mouth non-surgical periodontal scaling vs untreated
intervention_description: An untimed single episode of non-surgical periodontal therapy comprising supra- and subgingival scaling using Gracey curettes and a piezoelectric ultrasonic device. Followed by a full-mouth dental prophylaxis using a rubber cup and Ainsworth prophylaxis paste. Local anaesthesia administered as required. Also received oral hygiene advice consisting of toothbrush and flossing instructions and provided with a toothbrush and toothpaste.

comparison_summary: full-mouth non-surgical periodontal scaling vs untreated
intervention_description: Untreated control where periodontal intervention was delayed for 12 months. Received oral hygiene advice consisting of toothbrush and flossing instructions and were provided with a toothbrush and toothpaste at baseline.

comparison_summary: full-mouth scaling and root planing vs no periodontal treatment
intervention_description: The patients received oral hygiene instructions and full-mouth scaling and root planing performed under local anaesthesia.

comparison_summary: full-mouth scaling and root planing vs no periodontal treatment
intervention_description: The control group received no periodontal treatment during the study period.

comparison_summary: periodontal treatment (intervention) vs non-periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: In the intervention group, mechanical debridement of the sub-gingival plaque and calculus was performed using piezo-electric ultra sonic scalers, and 10 mg of minocycline ointment (Periofil®, Showa Yakuhin Co., Tokyo, Japan) was administered topically in every periodontal pocket at the end of each visit.

comparison_summary: periodontal treatment (intervention) vs non-periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Control group participants received instructions for brushing their teeth, including the use of inter-proximal cleaning aids, such as floss and inter-dental brushes, depending on their individual needs.

comparison_summary: periodontal treatment arm vs delayed treatment arm
intervention_description: All participants received oral hygiene instructions at baseline. The IG received non-surgical periodontal therapy in the form of full-mouth scaling and root planing (SRP), in two sessions, 1 week apart, with the use of an ultrasonic scaler (Minipiezon Electromedical Systems EMS, Nyon, Switzerland) and hand instruments, under local anaesthesia. All subjects received oral hygiene instructions after each visit, while the IG received additional supportive SRP at each visit, if judged necessary.

comparison_summary: periodontal treatment arm vs delayed treatment arm
intervention_description: All participants received oral hygiene instructions at baseline. Patients in the CG (minimal treatment group) received periodontal prophylaxis at baseline, in the form of supragingival removal of all deposits (plaque and calculus) with an ultrasonic scaler. SRP was performed in the CG after the completion of the study.

comparison_summary: nonsurgical periodontal therapy in the form of scaling and root planning [SRP] vs no-treatment
intervention_description: oral hygiene instructions at baseline followed by nonsurgical periodontal treatment comprising four SRP sessions over a maximum of 2 weeks, using standard rigid Gracey curettes and an ultrasonic scaler

comparison_summary: nonsurgical periodontal therapy in the form of scaling and root planning [SRP] vs no-treatment
intervention_description: oral hygiene instructions at baseline followed by nonsurgical periodontal treatment comprising four SRP sessions over a maximum of 2 weeks, using standard rigid Gracey curettes and an ultrasonic scaler

comparison_summary: nonsurgical periodontal therapy in the form of scaling and root planning [SRP] vs no-treatment

intervention_description: Periodontal treatment was performed in the no-treatment group (NT group) after completion of the study (after 6 months).

comparison_summary: Early Treatment vs untreated (Usual Care)
intervention_description: Early Treatment for 4 months (periodontal scaling and root planing until smooth root surfaces were achieved plus doxycycline [100 mg by mouth daily for 14 days] and chlorhexidine gluconate [CHX] rinses [30 cc, 0.12%, twice daily for 4 months])

comparison_summary: Early Treatment vs untreated (Usual Care)
intervention_description: 'By Usual Care' we mean that the participants used did not alter their medical and dental care routine; rather, they proceeded with their health care as usual.

comparison_summary: oral hygiene instructions + scaling and root planing vs oral hygiene instructions + supragingival removal of plaque and calculus
intervention_description: All study participants were instructed in oral hygiene using the modified Bass technique. In addition, TG patients were treated by full-mouth debridement, which consisted of scaling and root planing (SRP).

comparison_summary: oral hygiene instructions + scaling and root planing vs oral hygiene instructions + supragingival removal of plaque and calculus
intervention_description: All study participants were instructed in oral hygiene using the modified Bass technique. Periodontal 4 was performed at baseline by removal supragingival deposits (plaque and calculus) using an ultrasonic scaler

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRPAT vs CTR
intervention_description: In the SRP group, supragingival scaling was performed only on the first visit by 2 trained dentists working together simultaneously. After 2 weeks, root planing was performed to remove the subgingival calculus.

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRPAT vs CTR
intervention_description: In the SRPAT group, additional toothbrushing (Watanabe method) with a 2-row toothbrush was applied on the first visit by a trained dentist. On the second visit, subgingival calculus was removed as appropriate according to the patient's oral health condition. Additional toothbrushing (Watanabe method) was performed once a week from the first visit through the fifth visit.

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRPAT vs CTR
intervention_description: The CTR group received no other treatments beyond medical screening for diabetes. However, all groups received oral health education including toothbrush instruction at the baseline visit

comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal treatment vs no periodontal treatment
intervention_description: Initially, all participants received one session of supra-gingival plaque removal and oral hygiene instructions. The non-surgical periodontal treatment consisted of at least 60 minutes of scaling and root planing using curettes and an ultrasonic instrument during 2 or more sessions completed within 42 days after the baseline visit. Three and 6 months after the baseline visit, participants in the treatment group received periodontal maintenance therapy including oral hygiene instructions and oral prophylaxis for approximately 1 hour during a single session.

comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal treatment vs no periodontal treatment
intervention_description: Initially, all participants received one session of supra-gingival plaque removal and oral hygiene instructions. Participants in the control group received only oral hygiene instructions at the baseline and 3 and 6 month visits.

comparison_summary: nonsurgical periodontal therapy verses oral hygiene instructions
intervention_description: All subjects were instructed in oral hygiene methods using a soft bristled toothbrush, a compact-tuft toothbrush, interdental brushes and dental floss (TePe® oral hygiene education set) utilizing the modified Bass technique. Plaque scores of the subjects in the NSPT group were reviewed at weekly intervals to achieve scores of 20% or below to a maximum of 3 weeks. Subjects were re-motivated and instructed when necessary. Assigned treatment for the NSPT group was full mouth debridement, which consisted of scaling and root planing, was done in a single visit for all subjects in the NSPT group using an ultrasonic scaler (SATELEC P5 Newtron XS, Acteon, Merignac, France) and Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy, Chicago, USA). Additionally, all subjects in the NSPT group were given a 0.12% Chlorhexidine mouthrinse (Hexipro®, Evapharm, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia). They were instructed to rinse three times a day using 15 ml each time for a period of 14 days commencing immediately after completion of full mouth debridement. Thereafter at each monthly recall visit, participants in both groups were reviewed and re-motivated. Professional prophylaxis comprising of scaling and polishing was performed only on subjects of the test group.

comparison_summary: nonsurgical periodontal therapy verses oral hygiene instructions
intervention_description: All subjects were instructed in oral hygiene methods using a soft bristled toothbrush, a compact-tuft toothbrush, interdental brushes and dental floss (TePe® oral hygiene education set) utilizing the modified Bass technique. No interventional treatment was given to the OHI group apart from oral hygiene instructions and motivation. Thereafter at each monthly recall visit, participants in both groups were reviewed and re-motivated.

comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal treatment vs delayed non-surgical periodontal treatment
intervention_description: motivational intervention helping patients change behavior associated with customized oral hygiene instructions for daily plaque control. At the end of the first phase, active professional treatment was carried out. Scaling and root planing were performed under local anesthesia and treatment was divided in four sessions within 24 h, each of 45 min for quadrant and were performed using an ultrasonic scaler... and manual instruments... A continuous water spray on the working area was maintained, and a subgingival irrigation with an antiseptic mouthwash (chlorhexidine 0.12%) was associated.

comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal treatment vs delayed non-surgical periodontal treatment
intervention_description: At the end of the 6-month follow-up period the non-surgical periodontal treatment was carried out for the control group, performing the same procedures for an ethical reason.

comparison_summary: scaling and root planing (SRP) with metronidazole (MET) and oral hygiene instructions (OHI) vs SRP + OHI vs OHI only
intervention_description: Participants of test group-1 received SRP through a combination of ultrasonic scaling (average 60 min on medium intensity full mouth in single sitting) and hand instrumentation (using sharpened and sterilized curesttes) to smoothen irregular areas of root surface until the surfaces were smooth[20] followed by MET 400 mg × 3 for 10 days[12] along with warm salt water rinses for 3–5 days[21] and OHI.

comparison_summary: scaling and root planing (SRP) with metronidazole (MET) and oral hygiene instructions (OHI) vs SRP + OHI vs OHI only
intervention_description: Participants in test group-2 received the same intervention as test group-1 except MET.

comparison_summary: periodontal intervention vs no intervention
intervention_description: underwent no intervention

comparison_summary: periodontal treatment vs delayed periodontal treatment
intervention_description: The nonsurgical treatment was a full mouth debridement performed in a single visit consisting of scaling, root scaling and planning. This mechanical therapy was done using a magneto-restrictive ultrasonic device (Denjoy Dus-1A*, Changsha, China) and Gracey's cures followed by a sub-gingival irrigation with a 10% povidone iodine solution. Additionally, all the subjects of the treatment group received dental floss and chlorhexidine gluconate 0.2% as mouth wash (10 ml twice daily for 5 days).

comparison_summary: periodontal treatment vs delayed periodontal treatment
intervention_description: No interventional treatment was given to the control group during the follow up, apart from the oral hygiene instructions.

comparison_summary: oral hygiene instruction (OHI), scaling and root debridement vs OHI alone
intervention_description: professional oral hygiene instruction, while non-surgical periodontal therapy was only performed for the Treatment group, including extraction of hopeless teeth, scaling and root debridement with both hand instruments and ultrasonic scaler.

comparison_summary: oral hygiene instruction (OHI), scaling and root debridement vs OHI alone
intervention_description: professional oral hygiene instruction... Similar treatment was provided for the Control group after completion of the study.

comparison_summary: "immediate" vs "delayed" periodontal treatment
intervention_description: Periodontal treatment included non-surgical scaling and root planing (SRP), systemic antibiotics (amoxicillin 2 g/day for 7 days after periodontal treatment) and providing a supply of oral hygiene products and oral health instructions. Dental surgeons who were specially trained by an experienced periodontist prior to the launch of the study performed full-mouth ultrasonic and hand instrument debridement. Local anaesthesia was administered if necessary. SRP was accompanied by subgingival irrigation with an antiseptic mouthwash (chlorhexidine 0.12%).

comparison_summary: "immediate" vs "delayed" periodontal treatment
intervention_description: Delayed periodontal treatment for the control group was performed with exactly the same procedures at the end of the 3-month follow-up period. Therefore, the control group was a true "no treatment" control arm for which no periodontal procedure was performed during the follow-up.

comparison_summary: T2DM-T group vs T2DM-NT group
intervention_description: without periodontal intervention

comparison_summary: T2DM-T group vs T2DM-NT group
intervention_description: Periodontal intervention included oral hygiene, full-mouth scaling (supragingival and subgingival scaling), root planning, periodontal flap surgery when indicated, and extraction of hopeless teeth, restore of balanced occlusion. Antibiotics (Tinidazole 1.0 g, bid, po. and ampicillin 0.25 g, qid, po.) were prescribed for 3 days before and after periodontal intervention.

comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal treatment vs temporarily without periodontal treatment
intervention_description: intensive oral health instruction and supragingival scaling and polishing were performed. In the following up appointment, oral hygiene was monitored and reinforced. Subgingival scaling and root planning was carried out under topical anesthesia on a quadrant-by-quadrant basis. Each subject was prescribed doxycycline in a dose of 100 mg/day for 14 days.

arm_label: group B: temporarily without periodontal treatment
comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal treatment vs temporarily without periodontal treatment
intervention_description: Group B acted as a non-treatment control group for the duration of the study, and then they were treated in exactly the same manner as described for group A. Each subject was prescribed doxycycline in a dose of 100 mg/day for 14 days.

comparison_summary: periodontal surgery vs supportive periodontal treatment
intervention_description: In group A, modified Widman flap procedures were performed in the areas where there were deep pockets. Following reverse incisions, full thickness mucoperiosteal flaps were raised, granulation tissue removed, root instrumentation performed and alveolar bone shape corrected. The flaps were replaced to their original position and secured with sutures which were removed 1 week after surgery.

comparison_summary: periodontal surgery vs supportive periodontal treatment
intervention_description: In group B, scaling and root planning was taken in the diseased root surfaces. Subjects were advised to rinse with 0.2% chlorhexidine solution twice daily for 2 weeks.

comparison_summary: SRP vs untreated control and ERP vs prophylaxis
intervention_description: Patients in the treatment group underwent oral health instructions, supra-/subgingival scaling (Cavitron Bobcat Pro, Dentsply, York, PA, USA), and manual curettage (Hu-Friedy, Chicago, IL, USA)

comparison_summary: SRP vs untreated control and ERP vs prophylaxis
intervention_description: The control group was not given any periodontal treatment except for evaluations at the baseline as well as on the 3rd and 6th months.

comparison_summary: SRP vs untreated control and ERP vs prophylaxis
intervention_description: Patients in the sub-ERP group again received full-month ultrasonic scaling and manual root planing of the teeth with PPD $\geq 4$ mm.

comparison_summary: SRP vs untreated control and ERP vs prophylaxis
intervention_description: the subprophylaxis group received only full-month ultrasonic scaling to remove calculus and plaque.
